articles.headline: Guardiola's return, Man City's defiance - and a game of glorious chaos
keyFacts: Manchester City showed a united front at home following their financial breach verdict, with Pep Guardiola attending in support of club leadership.
Paris St-Germain dominated the first half to build a three-goal lead, ultimately defeating Manchester City 4-2 in a chaotic Champions League match.
Manager Enzo Maresca stated he was happy with his team's second-half response, and Manchester City will next face Ipswich Town domestically.
body: Manchester City returned to the welcoming surroundings of home for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations awash with defiance and presenting an 'us against the world' united front.

Pep Guardiola was back at the place he decorated with success for a decade in a public show of support to embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano, the Catalan a low-key presence clad in a flat cap sitting a row behind the pair.
If his appearance was relatively under the radar, the fact that he chose a game certain to attract a global audience to make his return was heavy with significance.
Guardiola is ignoring the outside noise to back his former bosses to clear their name on appeal after the guilty verdict passed down by an independent commission.
The stand bearing his name was emblazoned with a 'CTID' - City 'Til I Die - mosaic, while the build-up to kick-off saw a display of fireworks and pyrotechnics worthy of several rock concerts.

The strategy to show an unabashed City ready to face down any enemy was going well, until the game kicked off and Champions League holders Paris St-Germain produced a ruthless first-half reality check cloaked within the brutal beauty of their football.
With City providing a dramatic backdrop off the pitch, the game more than matched the setting. A second-half revival ensured embarrassment was avoided - and instead gave us a classic.
Man City suffer as PSG masterclass sets up Champions League win
How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team?
City's first step back into the limelight on the hostile territory of Anfield on Sunday ended with a 3-0 win at Liverpool and wild celebrations.

Here, with Guardiola watching on from the directors' box with an agonised expression mirroring that of successor Enzo Maresca in his technical area, City ran headlong into a whirlwind of magnificent football from Luis Enrique's PSG, the half-time scoreline of 3-0 actually doing them a kindness.
To City's great credit, and also Maresca's after he made three half-time changes, they responded superbly after the break, creating a host of chances before eventually losing 4-2.
It did not retrieve what was lost in the first half, but it did at least allow City's fans to ramp up a frenzied atmosphere and give their team a rousing send-off at the final whistle.

In these surroundings, there was no question of any backlash against City's Abu Dhabi-based owners, despite the fact they were found guilty of such serious financial charges to leave the club in crisis and attracting pariah status.
The damage was done in PSG's staggering opening 45 minutes, with Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha the scorers as City were ripped apart.
A game that began in a wall of sound, with Guardiola's name resounding around the stadium at kick-off, was reduced to stunned silence in the first 15 minutes.
City, so composed and ordered amid the toxicity of Anfield on Sunday, were shell-shocked on home territory as even born streetfighters such as Enzo Fernandez were reduced to chasing shadows.

The players who rose in the face of the storm raging around Manchester City at Liverpool suddenly looked like they were carrying the weight of the world on their shoulders, which made their outstanding display after the break even more praiseworthy.
Guardiola looked just as engaged as when he was manager

Pep Guardiola appeared to go through every motion during Manchester City's 4-2 defeat [Getty Images] Erling Haaland gave City hope, which looked to be snuffed out when goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who had a very poor night against his former club, saved from Maghnes Akliouche, only to see the ball drop behind him into the net.
Guardiola sometimes looked just as engaged as he did when he prowled the touchline here at Etihad Stadium, collecting the trophies now being called into question.

When Josko Gvardiol had a header cleared off the line Guardiola clutched his face in anguish. When Haaland scored a goal that threatened to offer City an unlikely lifeline, he remained seated but pumped his fists into the air.
If the Catalan was a neutral observer, he would have relished a game of glorious chaos, the first half embellished by PSG before City mounted superb momentum after the break.
As a lover of pure football with the emphasis placed firmly on attack, he may have enjoyed it anyway. The post-match discussion with Maresca would certainly have had a busy agenda.
Maresca felt he saw enough to give City hope should they meet PSG again later in the Champions League, despite the manner in which they were dismantled in the first half.

"I really like playing against PSG because they are brave," said Maresca. "We know the way they want to press. They go man-to-man and they are very dynamic on the ball. They are the best team in Europe. They play fantastic football.

"But I think we are there. The reason why we struggled was because we conceded two early goals so quickly. When you are on the pitch you might think this is difficult, but in the second half we created enough to maybe deserve something.
"We feel sorry for the first half but I think we're quite happy now."
'Goals, goals and more goals'
Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha, watching for Match of the Day, described it as "great entertainment", but "not a normal game of football".

"I don't feel like both teams were going at it at the same time," he said. "In the first half, PSG were excellent and City looked really off the pace. As a consequence they were heavily punished and the game basically left them.

"But then in the second half they have made some changes, they have rallied, knowing they are playing in front of their own crowd and their performance had to be better. So, it was more aggressive and more on the front foot, and that's why we saw those crazy scenes where it was shot after shot by City.

"If these two teams had played this game in matchweek six or seven, it would not have looked like this. There would have been more defensive solidity from both sides and they would probably have approached the game in a different manner.
"But at this stage, as we have kind of seen with some of the other games tonight, it is just goals, goals and more goals."

Either way, the superb Enrique remains the scourge of the Premier League, adding another win against City to a Champions League victims list that includes Liverpool, Aston Villa, Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal, in a semi-final then last season's final.
Enrique is currently master of all he surveys in Europe as leader of this wonderful PSG team.

For Maresca and City, it is back to domestic business at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday – and all the uncertainty that brings with the Premier League in a state of limbo as they await sanctions and the result of their appeal.

articles.headline: Kamala Harris calls for packing Supreme Court, ‘changing’ Electoral College if Dems take back congress
keyFacts: Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for expanding the Supreme Court and changing the Electoral College during a podcast interview.
Attorney Y. David Scharf warned that Harris's proposed changes set a dangerous precedent, while Democratic strategists voiced skepticism about her future.
Harris stated she remains undecided about running for president in 2028 while urging support for Democrats in the upcoming midterms.
body: Kamala Harris calls for packing Supreme Court, ‘changing’ Electoral College if Dems take back congress
By
Hanna Panreck, Fox News
Published Oct. 14, 2026, 4:10 p.m. PT
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris called for institutional changes to the Supreme Court and the Electoral College during an interview Tuesday, calling for more justices on the highest court in the nation.

“The work that we can do about winning back the House and the Senate is going to be on a number of things. For example, I believe that we need to expand the Supreme Court. We need more justices on the Supreme Court so that we can have a court that actually reinforces the spirit and principles behind the Constitution of the United States,” Harris told podcast host Keke Palmer on her “Baby, This is Keke Palmer” podcast.
“I believe that we should be pushing for what is possible around changing the Electoral College. Right?

“It’s about, the popular vote has to matter, right? You know, all the things that make people feel, like, overwhelmed, and does their vote matter? We have, you know, listen, if the folks there want it, we should be pushing for statehood for Puerto Rico and D.C., right? These are some of the things that are structural that we need to do, but we need to reestablish affordable child care,” Harris added.
Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in 2024. She told Palmer she still remains undecided about a 2028 presidential run.
Y. David Scharf, chairman of Morrison Cohen LLP and head of its government strategies & controversies practice, told Fox News Digital that Harris’ proposed changes could set a “dangerous precedent.”

“Kamala Harris says she wants to defend democracy, but her solution is to rewrite its rules when Democrats don’t like the results. That’s a dangerous precedent,” he said. “Nine justices have been the number since 1869. FDR tried to pack the Supreme Court, and even his own party pushed back. Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg herself warned that expanding the court would make it look partisan.

“The Electoral College is written into the Constitution. Eliminating it requires a constitutional amendment, not a Democratic majority in Congress. You don’t get to change the referee because you don’t like the calls. Harris may think this is a winning message for the Democratic base, but it’s a much tougher sell to the independent and swing voters her party needs.”

“On the first Tuesday in November, the midterms are going to happen,” Harris said. “And our ability to put people in Congress who will say no, when they do things like cut $1 trillion out of Medicaid will be powerful and affect people right away.

“Our ability to put people in Congress who will say enough of the corruption, enough of ending the funding for research on issues like fibroids, which they have done under the guise of attacking DEI, can be stopped. There are things that are not only about what will be helpful, but also stopping what is harmful, that we can do right away with these midterm elections.”

Her comments come days after her 2024 vice presidential running mate, Gov. Tim Walz, warned of a reckoning among Democrats if the party fails to deliver on promises should they take back Congress and potentially the presidency in 2028.
Harris was called out by Democratic advisors Tuesday for failing to reinvent herself politically as she weighs another White House run, Politico reported.

The report, based on interviews with nearly 20 California-based Democratic donors and strategists, highlighted growing skepticism among some party insiders about Harris’ political future and whether she has done enough to distinguish herself from her unsuccessful 2024 campaign.
Longtime Democratic strategist Doug Herman, a veteran of former President Barack Obama’s 2008 and 2012 campaigns, told Politico that Harris “totally blew it. … She hasn’t gotten into the mix.”

Former Gov. Jim Hodges of South Carolina, the leadoff state in the Democratic Party’s 2028 presidential nominating calendar, told the outlet, “I don’t see anything different myself. It seems like more of the same to me.”

Veteran Democratic strategist Maria Cardona, an outside advisor to Harris, pushed back against the criticism highlighted in a new Politico report and called the story “infuriating” in a previous statement to Fox News Digital.

“How can you state that she hasn’t done anything new or groundbreaking or talked about new initiatives or policies and then lay out exactly those policies — like proposing an expanded Supreme Court, lowering the voting age to 16, making D.C. and Puerto Rico states. Those are pretty groundbreaking policies,” Cardona told Fox News Digital, as she pointed to some of Harris’ moves since the end of former President Joe Biden’s administration.
Fox News’ Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Wannabe LA mayor Nithya Raman claims she went into a ‘fugue state’ during Karen Bass debate
keyFacts: Mayoral challenger Nithya Raman claimed she entered a 'fugue state' and did not remember her debate with Mayor Karen Bass.
Licensed therapist Dr. Azita Sayan stated concern that Raman could be using the psychiatric term as a political excuse.
The confrontation occurred with three weeks remaining in the Los Angeles mayoral race between Raman and incumbent Bass.
body: Nithya Raman claimed she went into a “fugue state” and did not remember her Los Angeles mayoral debate with Karen Bass.
The challenger made the remark in a bizarre interview with NBC4 just moments after leaving the stage in Universal City on Tuesday night.
According to the National Institutes of Health, a fugue state “is one of the rare psychiatric disorders characterized by sudden unexpected travelling from one’s customary place of living or work.”
The NIH website adds: “Traumatic circumstances, leading to an altered state of consciousness dominated by a wish to flee, are thought to be the underlying cause.”
NBC’s Robert Kovacik opened his post-debate interview with Raman asking: “Let’s go through the debate. Here’s your moment, your strongest tonight and your weakest moment tonight.”
She replied: “Oh, you know, to be honest with you, I’m so sorry but I was in fugue state and I don’t remember very much of it at all.”
Dr. Azita Sayan, CEO of Embrace Growth Inc. a licensed family therapist with a PhD in psychology, said she was concerned the term was being used “as a political out.”
She told The Post: “My concern would be if it gets used as a political out.”

Dr. Sayan said she could not determine from Raman’s remarks whether she had experienced a dissociative fugue, and acknowledged people sometimes use the phrase casually to describe feeling overwhelmed.

She said the clinical condition involves unexpected travel or wandering of the mind accompanied by significant memory loss about someone’s identity or personal history — far more than difficulty recalling a stressful debate.
“Imagine finding yourself somewhere unfamiliar and being unable to remember who you are or how you got there,” she said.

People experiencing a dissociative fugue may appear outwardly normal while feeling confused about their identity, Dr Sayan said. Some assume a different identity, although not everyone forgets their entire past.
The American Psychological Association classifies dissociative fugue as a feature of dissociative amnesia rather than a separate diagnosis.
Sayan questioned whether that description matched what Raman had publicly recounted.
“In this case, the person knew who they are, they knew where they were,” she said. “They didn’t forget their identity.”
But she emphasized that the candidate’s choice of words was not enough to draw a clinical conclusion.
“What I would want to ask Nithya Raman is, what does she mean by a fugue state?” Sayan said.
“People sometimes use that phrase to describe feelings of being overwhelmed or barely remembering a stressful experience.”
Sayan said overwhelming stress or trauma can precede the condition. She also raised the possibility of someone invoking the term to explain a mistake or an answer they could not defend.
“It could also be an excuse,” she said. Her broader concern, she said, was that using a clinical term as political cover could undermine people experiencing actual symptoms.
“Then if someone genuinely has a problem, then we no longer believe them,” Sayan said.
An account called No Show Nithya seized on Raman, suggesting she could simply just struggle under pressure.
It posted: “Ah yes, exactly what we need, a mayoral candidate who blacks out when she gets stressed. That’ll go really well.”
Other users turned their criticism toward Bass, defending Raman for taking questions after the debate.
“No one blanks out when stressed better than Karen Bass does. At least Nithya took questions after the debate. Karen had to run and hide as usual,” one X user wrote.
It is not clear if Raman has ever been diagnosed with suffering the condition or if her comments to Kovacik were flippant.
The post-debate exchange followed a tense confrontation between the former political allies, who traded sharp attacks with just three weeks remaining in the LA mayoral race.
Raman accused Bass of presiding over worsening homelessness, struggling businesses and wasted taxpayer dollars.

“We cannot afford another four years of decline, of mismanagement of excuses. homelessness is rising despite hundreds of millions of dollars spent. storefronts are closing. Our tax money is being wasted, and through it all, we’ve had a mayor who has been MIA,” said Raman.
Bass countered by questioning Raman’s leadership and ability to prepare Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympics.

“We are 640 days away from the greatest sporting event in U.S. history, and I believe that the city would be destabilized with someone who has extreme views and basically has not been able to build relationships, not on city council and not with her constituents. Now is not the time to turn the city over to Nithya Raman,” said Bass.
Bass has never lost an election during a political career spanning Sacramento, Washington, D.C., and Los Angeles.
Raman, once a Bass ally, upended the race in February when she announced her bid to unseat the mayor and entered the primary field.

articles.headline: How much money does FIFA pay to member associations? Gianni Infantino reportedly has plan to distribute $6 billion
keyFacts: FIFA president Gianni Infantino reportedly proposed a plan to distribute $6 billion to member associations between 2027 and 2030.
The proposal follows public calls from soccer officials to increase payouts following the financial success of the 2026 World Cup.
The plan requires approval from the FIFA Council and ratification by the FIFA Congress to take effect.
body: Gianni Infantino has been under heavy fire since the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
The FIFA president's position has been in serious question since the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise plan put a target on his back.

With a new presidential election coming up in March, the pressure on his position has called into question his viability of winning another term, able to run for one more four-year presidency before FIFA statutes prevent him from running again.

The commercial and financial success of the 2026 FIFA World Cup has enriched the organization even further, growing the non-profit's cash reserves which have already reached into the billions. Amidst calls to distribute that wealth amongst the member nations to grow the game globally, Infantino has devised a plan to put that money back into the game as the elections approach.
How much money does FIFA distribute to member associations?

Through the last four-year World Cup cycle, a period from 2023 to 2026, FIFA paid out approximately $1.76 billion in total to its member nations, which comes out to around $8.3 million per nation across the four years.

After the commercial success of the 2026 World Cup, UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF head Victor Montagliani have both publicly called on FIFA to increase that total to at least $10 million per member for the next four-year cycle.
Infantino's plan to pay out $6 billion to associations
According to a report by Dan Sheldon of The Athletic on October 13, Gianni Infantino has devised a plan to increase FIFA's distribution of wealth to member associations in the coming years.
The proposal would reportedly see a total of $6 billion distributed across member associations between 2027 and 2030, more than double what would normally have been handed out during that time.
Each member association would receive a total of $25 million over the four-year cycle, with an additional $99 million distributed to each continental confederation as well.
To accomplish this, FIFA would dip into its sizable financial reserves, distributing $3.5 billion from its coffers.

In order to take effect, this plan would first need to be approved by the FIFA Council at its meeting this Thursday, October 15, and then would need to be ratified by the FIFA Congress, which convenes in March. This plan, therefore, is likely not contingent upon Infantino's re-election, which would also take place at that same event.

body: Motor sports have skyrocketed in popularity over the last few years, which has brought mainstream sports fans to F1 betting and NASCAR betting through pop culture, including the Daytona 500 and a variety of upcoming grand prix races in F1. We'll take a look at motor sports betting strategies, F1 betting tips, and the best F1 betting sites.
Finding the best sportsbook promos for motor sports betting
Here's a look at some of the promotions going on at top sportsbooks for fans interested in getting into motor sports betting.

The , FanDuel, and the are all offering "bet and get" promotions where users receive bonus bets after an initial wager, making them popular F1 betting apps. DraftKings and FanDuel both require $5 to get started — DraftKings rewards new users with $200 in bonus bets and three months of NBA League Pass after $5 are spent, while FanDuel returns up to $350 in bonuses if the user bets $5 for seven days, with a bonus bet token allotted for each $5 bet. Lastly, Fanatics offers $350 in FanCash after a $20 wager.

The structures its offers around what happens after you place your first bet. BetMGM covers a user's first bet up to $1,500 with bonus bets if that first bet loses, but users must wager at least $1,500 to be eligible for the full amount.
Caesars Sportsbook offers new users up to $250 in bet reset tokens.

Before you get into motor sports betting, it's important to find a sportsbook that consistently provides odds for races. All of the above sportsbooks have established themselves as strong F1 betting sites, almost always allowing their users to bet on F1. There's always value in shopping around multiple sportsbooks for the best lines, but some platforms do not offer extensive betting markets for motorsports compared to others.
Prediction markets and motor sports

Popular prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket have motor sports markets available to trade. As federally regulated markets, they are both widely available throughout the United States, giving interested fans easier access to motor sports trading. Additionally, both offer new users signup bonuses that are outlined below.

Kalshi's offer is an appealing one. New users who make an initial trade of $25 or more receive $55 in bonus trading credits. Kalshi is available nationwide for new users to sign up. It is important to note that sports contracts are currently unavailable in MI, NV, and WA. In order to be eligible for Kalshi's sign-up bonus, new users must be physically located in a state where Kalshi prediction markets operate and complete the sign-up and identity verification process.
Polymarket's offer is similar. Users who deposit $10 receive $25 in trading credits.
What do motor sports odds mean?

When it comes to motorsports and racing markets, odds are displayed and read similarly to how they are for most sports. Let's say a driver is priced at -150 to win the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7th, and the next best driver has +200 odds. That means the driver at -150 is a decent favorite to win, and you'd have to risk $150 to win $100. The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.
When you can bet on motor sports odds

The racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.

Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.
Biggest races for motor sports betting
Arguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.

NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.

Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.
Types of bets and how motor sports betting works
Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.
Outright/To win odds

This market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.
Here are the odds to win the United States Grand Prix, taking place on October 25, 2026. Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook and are current as of October 14, 2026.
- Max Verstappen +115
- Andrea Kimi Antonelli +230
- George Russell +1000
- Lewis Hamilton +1200
- Lando Norris +1200
Placement/Top Finish odds

Motor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.

While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.
Dual Forecast

This is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.
Each Way Betting

This is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.
Stage Winner

This is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.
Matchups/Head-to-Head

Sportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.
Group Winner
This is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.
Top Car Make Driver

This is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.
Team of Race Winner
This is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.
Qualifying Bets

Bettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.
Motor sports futures betting
Formula 1 betting

In most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.
NASCAR Betting

NASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.
IndyCar
The major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.
Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?

While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.
How to bet on motor sports live during a race

Sportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.
Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sports

Driver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers.

Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.

Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.

Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed.

There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.
FAQ
Can you bet on motor sports?
As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.
Who to bet on for the Indy 500?

Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.

SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.
Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?
DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. You must be of legal age and residing in those states to bet on motocross at DraftKings.
How to bet on F1?
All major sportsbooks have lines available for F1 races. Many of the same types of bets available for NASCAR races are available for F1 events.

articles.headline: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez released a statement clarifying his criticism of the club's hierarchy after a Champions League defeat, but he did not apologize.
Martinez stated that his post-match outburst criticizing technical director Jason Wilcox and the club's transfer strategy stemmed from anger and frustration.
Club officials have not yet decided whether to discipline Martinez, while the boardroom and dressing room reacted with anger and bemusement.
body: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise

Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox
Wednesday 14 October 2026 23:53, UK
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.
But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.
- Lisandro Martinez outburst Q&A: Wilcox, transfer strategy and what next
- 'Awful' and 'disrespectful' - Carra and Rooney criticise Martinez outburst
- Martinez's Man Utd future in doubt after comments
He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.
"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.
"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.
"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."
Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:
There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.
United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.
Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.
It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.
The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.
Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.
No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.
The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".
Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.

articles.headline: Denmark pushes back as Trump touts Greenland oil and mineral deals
keyFacts: Denmark stated that a recent agreement does not grant US investors preferential resource access, contradicting President Donald Trump's claims of imminent extraction.
The agreement signed by Denmark, Greenland, and the United States expands American military access without allocating any mining or drilling rights.
Greenland's government is reviewing whether a Texas firm can use permits predating a 2021 ban to drill for oil in 2027.
body: Denmark has demanded that US resource exploration in Greenland respect the island’s laws amid President Donald Trump’s claim that oil, gas and mineral extraction will soon begin there.
The Danish Foreign Ministry reaffirmed on Wednesday that last month’s agreement between Denmark, Greenland and the US did not alter the rules for extraction.

The agreement “does not grant investors from the US any preferential treatment” over investors from other NATO and EU countries when it comes to access to natural resources in Greenland, the ministry said.
In a post on Truth Social, US President Trump called the semi-autonomous Danish territory “our new and beautiful Greenland”.
“Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin,” he wrote, without providing details.
What the deal covers

Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland’s Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the 10-page agreement on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 22, ending months of tensions over Trump’s threats to control Greenland.
The deal allows the US to “modernise and expand” its activities at the Pituffik Space Base, a remote US military installation in northwest Greenland.
It also paved the way for two new military bases and Trump’s “Golden Dome” missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.
It did not allocate any rights for mining or drilling.
Greenland’s ban
Greenland banned uranium mining and all future oil exploration in 2021.
Its government is reviewing whether a Texas firm, Greenland Energy, can use permits that predate the ban.
The company said in August it planned to drill for oil in 2027 at an untested basin on Greenland’s east coast, although it lacked its own permit.
Danish security policy adviser Jacob Kaarsbo said Trump’s comments could signal that his desire to control Greenland remains unchanged.
“It is extremely dangerous to view this agreement between the Trump administration and Denmark as something that has altered Trump’s intentions,” he said.

Mikkel Olesen, a senior researcher at the Danish Institute for International Studies, told Al Jazeera that details regarding mining and exploration rights remained unclear and that information coming mostly from the US side should be taken “with a grain of salt”.
Richard Weitz, a fellow at the NATO Defense College in Rome, said Trump “backed down and settled for less” than he sought, but still “got pretty much everything he wanted, except formal annexation”.

articles.headline: Intero Biosystems wants drugmakers to test on mini human intestines, not animals
keyFacts: Startup Intero Biosystems is selling lab-grown human intestinal organoids to help companies test drugs without using animal models.
Intero’s multi-tissue organoids mimic human biology more accurately than animal models to help reduce drug failures, founders said.
Intero plans to automate its manufacturing to produce hundreds of thousands of organoids per batch, CEO Charlie Childs said.
body: Drug development has long relied on animal models, but differences between species mean what works in animals doesn’t always translate to humans, and most drugs still fail during development. Intero Biosystems, a Denver-based startup, is developing human intestinal organoids, lab-grown tissue that mimics the gut, as another way to study how drugs and other compounds might affect the human body before they are tested in people. Researchers and pharmaceutical companies are increasingly looking for models that better reflect human biology to supplement animal testing and reduce their reliance on it.

Intero, which spun out of the University of Michigan, says its organoids differ from simpler models that replicate only part of the gut. They contain multiple cell and tissue types found in the human intestine, which the company believes makes them a more human-relevant model for testing drugs and other compounds, co-founder and CTO Madeline Eiken told TechCrunch.
“Most drugs fail clinical trials, and I think it’s pretty easy to appreciate that we are neither mice nor flat layers of cells,” Eiken said.

The startup’s flagship product, GastroScreen, is a human intestinal organoid model that it sells to pharmaceutical, biotech, food, and chemical companies for testing drugs and other compounds. Each organoid is about one millimeter across, and the company ships roughly 100 at a time in a tube, co-founder and CEO Charlie Childs said. Customers can use them as healthy intestinal models or induce disease-like conditions to test how the tissue responds to different compounds.
“We’re literally shipping mini living organs in the mail to people,” Childs said.

Beyond the organoids themselves, Intero sells the supplies needed to grow and work with them, such as the nutrient mixes that feed the cells and the chemicals used in experiments. It also runs studies for customers, including designing custom experiments, performing lab tests, and delivering the resulting data. Much of this work focuses on drug safety and disease research. For example, a customer can expose the organoids to a drug candidate to see whether it could harm the gut, or use organoids modeling a gut condition to see how the tissue responds to a compound.

Founded in 2024, the startup now has seven employees and just under 10 customers after raising a $2.3 million pre-seed round last year. It generated more than $400,000 in revenue from the fourth quarter of last year through the third quarter of this year, the CEO noted.

Regulatory changes have also helped drive interest in alternatives to animal testing. In April of last year, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) laid out plans to reduce its reliance on animal testing in drug development, promoting alternatives including organoids, organs-on-chips (small devices that mimic organ functions) and AI-based computational models as potential alternatives.

In March of this year, the FDA issued draft guidance outlining how drug developers should validate new approach methodologies, or NAMs, a term of non-animal testing methods, when using them to support regulatory submissions. The guidance provides a framework for validation but doesn’t endorse any specific method. Whether a NAM can support a submission depends on factors including the method, how it is used, and the data provided.

Changes in U.S. law that allow drug developers to use non-animal testing methods in some cases have made pharmaceutical companies more willing to explore technologies such as organoids, Eiken told TechCrunch. Companies once hesitant about the technology are now looking to bring organoids in-house, she added.

Intero isn’t alone in trying to build more human-relevant models of the gut. Altis Biosystems develops stem cell-derived intestinal models, while InSphero offers patient-derived intestinal organoids for gastrointestinal toxicity testing. Other peers like MIMETAS take a different approach with organ-on-chip technology, using microfluidic systems to recreate aspects of the environment inside human tissues.

Intero says it sets itself apart from competitors in the complexity and scalability of its model. Unlike intestinal models grown from tissue collected through procedures such as colonoscopies, GastroScreen is derived from induced pluripotent stem cells, which are adult cells reprogrammed to become almost any cell type and can be generated from a blood sample, Eiken explained. That approach gives the startup the potential to personalize its models to different patients and scale production more easily, she added.

When asked what evidence shows GastroScreen can predict human drug responses more accurately than existing animal or cell-based models, Childs said the company is still building that evidence and is now in the second stage of a three-stage validation process. Having first shown that GastroScreen contains the key tissues of the human gut, Intero is now testing well-known drugs with documented effects in humans. GastroScreen has shown expected responses to drugs that reduce intestinal inflammation and to compounds known to damage the gut, Childs told TechCrunch. In the final stage, the company will compare GastroScreen’s results directly with pharmaceutical companies’ existing animal and clinical data. Those studies are underway with several pharmaceutical companies, using both existing compounds and new drug candidates, Childs said.

Intero doesn’t use AI to build its organoids. Instead, Childs sees an opportunity to use the organoids to generate the biological data AI models need, and the company plans to license such datasets to pharmaceutical and AI companies.

In the near term, Intero is focused on scaling production. It can currently make a few thousand organoids at a time and is working to automate manufacturing, with the goal of producing hundreds of thousands per batch, Childs said. Longer term, it wants to move into personalized medicine, using a patient’s cells to create organoids that could test different drugs before treatment. Its most ambitious goal is an artificial intestine, a vision that Childs said would build on the manufacturing scale and patient-specific data generated through its organoid technology.

Intero took the stage earlier Wednesday at TechCrunch Disrupt, where it’s one of 20 startups vying for this year’s Startup Battlefield title. Join us for the rest of the action: Disrupt runs October 13 to 15 in downtown San Francisco.

articles.headline: Android Strengthens Scam Defenses for Calls and Texts
keyFacts: Google announced new Android security features utilizing artificial intelligence to block scam calls and text messages before they happen.
The updates include enhanced message protection, call-forwarding protection, and automatic hiding of sensitive login fields during screen sharing.
Google stated that these features will roll out over the next few weeks and later this year on various smartphone devices.
body: Google is launching new Android security features, including built-in protections for Google Messages and call forwarding, to block scams before they happen. In a blog post on Wednesday, the company said it’s using its AI technology to offer some of these protections and is already flagging 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month in its Phone and Google Messages apps.
The scam-detection updates include:

- An optional setting for Google Messages that enables an enhanced protection mode. This uses AI computing power, which Google says is handled privately with encryption on its servers, and can evaluate more of the message content to “understand a scammer’s intent more quickly when you’re in a conversation with an unknown sender.” It will also screen for malicious links and unfamiliar numbers. This option isn’t immediately available. Google says it will roll out over the next few weeks.
- Later this year, Google will bring scam detection to chat notifications on smartphones from other manufacturers, including Motorola, OnePlus and Xiaomi, as well as on its Pixel devices.

- Screen sharing will prevent sensitive info from being shown in login fields. For instance, if you’re screen sharing and need to enter a password, those fields will automatically be hidden to guard that information.

- Proactive call-forwarding protection will block apps from forwarding your calls without notifying you. This stops scammers from using call-forwarding tricks to intercept your passcodes and hijack accounts.

Google says it commissioned a study to gauge how concerned its users are about scams and found that 40% of the 4,500 adults who took a YouGov survey are “very” or “extremely” concerned about mobile fraud.
More from CNET
The updates could affect former users of Samsung Messages. That service shut down in July, and users were urged to switch to Google Messages.

articles.headline: Ex-Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan ignores everything about the hero shooter after his 'almost clinical' departure 5 years ago: 'I don't search for my name in Overwatch. I don't search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect.'
keyFacts: Former game director Jeff Kaplan told GameSpot he has completely avoided playing or following Overwatch since leaving Blizzard in 2021.
Kaplan stated he experienced an almost clinical separation from the game after previously going through a shocking departure from the World of Warcraft team in 2008.
Kaplan has now returned with a new studio to develop an open-world survival cowboy game called The Legend of California with former Blizzard developer Tim Ford.
body: Despite some big changes happening with Overwatch lately, former game director Jeff Kaplan hasn't touched it since the year he left Blizzard. In fact, he actively avoids the game in every way he can, he told GameSpot in a recent interview.

Before Overwatch, Kaplan rose through the ranks on the World of Warcraft team, starting in QA and eventually becoming game director. He described his departure from the WoW team in 2008 as "a training moment" for when he would leave the Overwatch team, and Blizzard altogether, in 2021.

"I kind of went through a little bit of shock leaving WoW back in 2008," Kaplan says. "So, when I stepped away from Overwatch in April of 2021, I was kind of used to that moment of what it meant to give all of yourself, your heart, your soul–because it's not just a job, there's no one who can do this and have it just be a job–and then have this shocking moment where you realize it doesn't belong to you. It belongs to the team, belongs to the players, it belongs to Blizzard, but it doesn’t belong to you."

Kaplan says he "had a very almost clinical separation" with Overwatch after what he went through with WoW. As a result, he stopped playing it the moment he left and has actively avoided it ever since.

"After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read," he says. "I don't watch YouTube [videos]. I don't search for my name in Overwatch. I don't search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, 'Yeah, I'm not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I'm the Overwatch guy, but like, that's just not for me anymore.'"

In an interview from earlier this year, Kaplan said he fully expected to retire from Blizzard, but the company's former CFO broke him by threatening to lay off 1,000 people if Overwatch didn't meet certain financial goals. Kaplan called that meeting "the biggest fuck you moment I've had in my career, it felt surreal to be in that condition."

Kaplan went quiet for several years before reappearing with a new studio and a new open world survival cowboy game called The Legend of California, which he's heading up alongside former Blizzard developer Tim Ford. He says the new game is an opportunity to explore something more personal to him for the first time. "I didn't leave Blizzard to try to make a Blizzard game. I left Blizzard to make a Tim and Jeff game."

keyFacts: Aston Villa secured their first home win of the season by defeating Fenerbahce 6-0 in a commanding Champions League match, manager Unai Emery said.
Nicolas Jackson scored two goals during the first half, contributing to a total of six goals scored by Aston Villa against the visitors.
Aston Villa will next play against Newcastle on Saturday as they attempt to improve their position in the Premier League.
body: - Published
Nicolas Jackson celebrated his first-half double by making a cutting motion which proved fitting on a night Aston Villa found their clinical edge.
A first win at Villa Park this season, three first-half goals with six in total and a commanding Champions League victory - all in the biggest European win in their history.
Unai Emery said his side had been impacted by the rebuild of the North Stand after three winless games at home this season but they showed no signs of struggle against Fenerbahce.
A dominant victory against the Turkish visitors leaves Villa already well placed to reach the Champions League knockout phase and will add to their slowly growing momentum.

Questions had been building as Villa picked up just one point from their opening three Premier League home games this season even if Saturday's 2-2 draw with Brentford ensured they avoided a third-straight home league defeat under Emery for the first time since February 2024.

Against Fenerbahce, they found a willing opponent. Scattered with former Premier League players, including Ederson, Nathan Ake, Romelu Lukaku and Nelson Semedo, the visitors would have been a formidable foe five years ago.
Instead, they folded quickly in the first half - despite Zion Suzuki's two important saves - as Johan Manzambi and Jackson's double put Villa in complete control.
The goals came in front of the skeleton of the North Stand, which will not have gone unnoticed as they had previously scored only once when attacking that end this season.
Ross Barkley's double and Tammy Abraham's late tap in added to the visitors' woes and underlined Villa's dominance.
They last scored so many in a 6-1 win over Brighton three years ago and had previously put five past Hibernian in the Europa Conference League in 2023.
The result provides another springboard and extends Villa's recent form to just one defeat in their last seven games.

However, Emery's rebuild will still take time. Before the international break, he described the opening five weeks of the campaign as similar to still being in pre-season with 10 new players to adapt following a chaotic summer of change.

Reflecting post match on how things are now progressing, he said: "They (Fenerbahce) didn't deserve 6-0 but for us it was very important how we achieved the first win at home and how we managed with different players, our progression and step forward.

"There is still a lot of work to do and we need time, we are progressively getting better and it was a good step forward. In the Champions League the three points are important. We want to be a protagonist in the Champions League.
"Now the clear objective is against Newcastle because of the lack of points in the Premier League."
The shoots of progress are already evident.
Manzambi glided past powerless Fenerbahce tackles, Ibraham Mbaye found space to exploit - even if he needs to improve - and Jackson was clinical.
Leon Goretzka made his debut as a late substitute and Suzuki remained commanding, continuing to slip into his role with ease.
"I think that's what Emery has been talking about with the potential of this team and what they can do," former Villa captain Stiliyan Petrov told TNT.

"There's been a lot of questions from the start of the season, even for this game as well. People asking how far they can go in this competition but it seems as though they're clicking together and there's a flow to their game.
"The players that Emery has brought in are starting to perform really well and it's a well-deserved win."
'Jackson is doing a fantastic job, fantastic task'
Record Â£65m signing Jackson came to replace the departing Ollie Watkins after his Â£50m switch to Al-Hilal.
He joined having helped Bayern Munich win the Bundesliga last season on loan from Chelsea, and on moving to Villa Park was reunited with Emery.
The pair worked together at Villarreal, with Emery giving him his debut with the Yellow Submarine.

The 25-year-old scored the final goal for Emery at Villarreal before the manager left for Villa in October 2022, a last-minute winner against Almeria, and has repaid the faith quickly on their reunion.
The only thing missing for Jackson was a potential hat-trick, with Barkley - the pre-arranged penalty taker - scoring from the spot.
"I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win. Hopefully next time I'll get the hat-trick," Jackson told TNT Sports.
"It's very important. We haven't won at home. Our keeper is amazing."

Jackson's four goals in three games and five for the season in total allow Villa and their fans to move on quickly from Watkins, their record Premier League scorer, following a summer exit that threatened to turn acrimonious.
Emery added: "Jackson is doing a fantastic job.
"He's scoring, he's working defensively [and] helping the team. This is very important and maybe in the future he can shoot (from the spot) as well."

Villa, and their new-look forward line, will now be eager for Saturday's trip to Newcastle, especially as Matthias Jaissle's side shipped four against Coventry on Monday to leave them with the joint-worst defensive record in the Premier League.
And Jackson hopes he can prosper alongside his attacking colleagues.

"He [Johan Manzambi] is a top player. I'm really happy we're playing together. I hope we score many more goals together," Jackson said. "[Ibrahim Mbaye] is [also] an amazing player. We're in the [Senegal] national team together and hopefully he'll get more time to play [for Villa]. He's very fast and it's good to have him."

body: President Donald Trump told rally attendees in Arizona on Wednesday to vote Republican in honor of the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk.

The president’s remarks came while stumping for Rep. Andy Biggs (R-AZ) and other downballot Republicans alongside the Arizona-Nevada border on Wednesday — the second stop of his three-legged 2026 campaign tour across western states.

“I also want to say a happy birthday to a great, great person, a great man, and a great friend of mine — a friend that helped me with our elections all the time,” the president stated near the end of his speech. “Thirty-three years old, he would be today, Charlie Kirk, the great Charlie Kirk.”

TRUMP SAYS GOVERNMENT LEAKERS ‘SHOULD BE SHOT’

articles.headline: Trump is taking his midterms anger out on Ukraine
keyFacts: Ukraine says its access to SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield satellite systems is being throttled amid growing tensions with President Donald Trump.
Starlink and Starshield provide vital battlefield communications and control drones used in Ukraine's military efforts against Russia.
The United States has reportedly threatened to suspend intelligence sharing if Ukraine conducts more strikes on Russian oil refineries.
body: Donald Trump walks to the White House from the South Lawn on October 10, 2026. | Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Is Trump turning on Ukraine?

What’s happening? Ukraine says its access to Starlink, the satellite internet system run by Elon Musk’s SpaceX company, and Starshield, the military version of the same technology, is being throttled as President Donald Trump’s animosity toward the country mounts.

Why is Trump angry with Ukraine? Trump has been hot and cold on Ukraine since he returned to office, but his current anger is driven by oil prices and successful Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries — particularly ahead of the US midterm elections.

Last week, Trump announced a US-Russia diesel deal, which has elicited bipartisan anger and probably won’t do much , if anything, for diesel prices in the US. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the deal, leading Trump to lash out and call for Zelenskyy’s replacement.

Over the weekend, Trump also announced an “ENERGY CEASEFIRE” between Ukraine and Russia that doesn’t really seem to exist . “Both parties have agreed,” he wrote. “Do not break it!” (Russia appears to have broken it the same day , while Ukraine is complying for now.)

Is Ukraine actually to blame for high oil prices? Partially, but not primarily; as the BBC explains , while Ukrainian refinery strikes play a role, ongoing disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf oil industry from Trump’s war with Iran have had a greater impact (though Trump has tried to shift the blame to Ukraine).

Why is Starlink so important? Starlink and Starshield provide vital communications infrastructure in Ukraine, especially on the battlefield. The technology is also used to control offensive and defensive Ukrainian drones, which have emerged as a key part of Ukraine’s military efforts against Russia.

What’s next? Despite the fact that neither Russia nor Ukraine seemingly signed on to Trump’s “ENERGY CEASEFIRE” and Russia is still attacking Ukrainian energy facilities , Trump is trying to bind Ukraine to it: The US has reportedly threatened to suspend US intelligence sharing, which has helped give Ukraine early warning of Russian missile attacks, if Ukraine strikes more Russian refineries.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: DOJ threatens emergency legal action against California over suspected noncitizen voters
keyFacts: The Justice Department demanded California election officials review potentially ineligible noncitizen voters and segregate their ballots, officials said.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta rejected the demands, stating there is no widespread voter fraud and accusing the administration of voter intimidation.
The Justice Department warned it will seek emergency legal relief if California officials do not comply by October 15.
body: The Justice Department is threatening emergency legal action against California election officials unless they take steps to prevent suspected noncitizens from voting in November's midterm elections, setting a Thursday deadline as state officials push back.

In letters sent Tuesday, Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter demanded that California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan review a list of potentially ineligible voters within 48 hours. The DOJ instructed officials to segregate ballots from individuals whose citizenship cannot be verified and warned it would seek emergency legal relief if its demands were not met by noon Eastern on Oct. 15.
A DOJ spokesperson told Fox News Digital that thousands of potential foreign nationals ineligible to vote have been identified on California's voter rolls statewide, not just in Los Angeles County.
MAP IT: DOJ ILLEGAL VOTING CRACKDOWN SWEEPS 17 STATES AS RAZOR-THIN ELECTIONS FACE SCRUTINY

"This should not be controversial, as the criminal statute is clear: only American citizens may vote in federal elections. It is a federal crime for noncitizens to vote in U.S. elections, and the DOJ is asking California to ensure that is not occurring," the spokesperson said.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta, a Democrat, pushed back during a Wednesday news conference, accusing the Trump administration of attempting to intimidate voters and promoting false allegations of widespread voter fraud .
JUSTICE DEPARTMENT CHARGES 16 ACROSS MULTIPLE STATES WITH ALLEGED ILLEGAL VOTING, ELECTION CRIMES
"There is no widespread voter preference, voter fraud problem. It doesn't exist. It is a lie. It is a conspiracy theory," Bonta said.
Bonta said his office is working with the secretary of state and Los Angeles County officials to review their options.
STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS
Meanwhile, Logan said his office received a password-protected USB drive purportedly containing voter records but has not accessed it because of cybersecurity concerns.

"We have not accessed the drive because doing so would conflict with established data privacy and information security protocols. We do not consider the device a secure medium. Additionally, the letter does not specify the number of individuals involved or describe the information contained in the records," he said.

The dispute comes as Californians are already casting ballots ahead of the Nov. 3 election. Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections , though the DOJ has not established that the individuals identified have cast illegal ballots.

articles.headline: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
keyFacts: Australia received its first Michelin stars, with 11 restaurants in South Australia being awarded the distinction.
Adelaide's Magill Estate Restaurant earned two stars, while 10 other South Australian restaurants received one star each.
South Australia's government paid for the Michelin inspection to promote the state as a global tourism destination, officials said.
body: - Published
Australia has been awarded its first Michelin stars, with 11 restaurants in the state of South Australia receiving the distinction.
Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide was the only venue to receive two stars, while 10 others were awarded one star each.
South Australia's government paid for incognito inspectors to visit the state, according to national broadcaster ABC, which is why no spots have been recognised in other parts of the country.
Magill chef and owner Scott Huggins said he had "dreamt of working in Michelin star restaurants as a youngster".
He said he had worked in Michelin star restaurants in Europe and Japan.
"It's one thing working for one, one thing achieving two [Michelin stars]," he said.
Wednesday's announcement comes more than a century after the Michelin Guide was first published in France and following years of unsuccessful attempts to bring it to Australia.
Michelin has approached the national tourism board about bringing the guide to the country more than once, with no luck.

South Australia decided to go it alone and pursued its own deal. The state government has not disclosed how much it paid, but Tourism Minister Emily Bourke defended the investment in an interview with ABC News.
"It is enabling us to create a tourism destination and put us on the world map," she said.

The move follows Michelin's expansion into New Zealand, which became the first destination in Oceania to feature in the guide in July, agreeing to pay NZ$6.3m (Â£2.7m; $3.5m) over three years for its inclusion.

Created by brothers AndrÃ© and Ãdouard Michelin in 1900, the guide was originally designed to encourage motorists to travel - ultimately boosting their core business of selling tyres. It offered drivers maps and recommendations for places to eat and stay, before evolving into one of the best-known names in restaurant recognition.
Michelin stars were introduced in 1926 and have since become a major distinction for chefs and restaurants around the world.
One star recognises high-quality cooking, two stars indicate excellent cooking worth a detour, while three stars are reserved for exceptional cuisine worth a special journey.

Among the one-star recipients is ArkhÃ© in Norwood, which specialises in open-fire cooking, while Aptos in Adelaide serves a tasting menu focused on native Australian ingredients. Here is the full list:

articles.headline: Xbox Considers Making Fallout, Elder Scrolls, and Minecraft Exclusive
keyFacts: Xbox leadership is surveying dedicated users about potentially making Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Minecraft exclusive to Microsoft platforms.
Call of Duty is exempt from potential exclusivity due to a 10-year multiplatform agreement signed by Microsoft in 2023.
The survey asks users where they would play future games if they were no longer available on PlayStation or Nintendo.
body: Under new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, Microsoft's gaming division has been instituting radical changes and reversals. These include laying off thousands of employees, shuffling around and divesting from some owned studios, and making some games Xbox console exclusives, such as Gears of War: E-Day. According to a new report, Xbox leadership is toying with additional exclusivity, including potentially making franchises like Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and even Minecraft only available on Microsoft's platforms.
The proposed changes sound dramatic and may never come to pass, but Xbox is floating the idea with its most dedicated users in a new survey, reports Windows Central.
Xbox is polling its biggest fans about new exclusives

According to Windows Central, Microsoft has distributed a survey to "a subset of Xbox users on the Insider Program" asking those users questions about where they would purchase future games in the Fallout, Elder Scrolls, and Minecraft franchises if they were no longer available on PlayStation or Nintendo platforms.
A screenshot of one of the survey questions reads as follows:

Imagine it was announced that all future title releases in the Fallout franchise will be console-exclusive to Xbox and no longer available on PlayStation or Nintendo. Existing Fallout titles would remain available where they are today. Nothing changes on PC with this announcement.
Under this scenario, which of the following best describes where you are MOST LIKELY to play any of this new exclusive content.
The survey then asks where they would play this exclusive content, with the following responses:
- On an existing Xbox I own
- On a new Xbox Series X|S I would decide to purchase
- On a PC
- I would skip playing because it would now be unavailable on my preferred console
- Something else (please specify)
- Not interested in playing this exclusive content

Another survey question posits a future where all releases "from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," including Minecraft, with the same responses. Currently, Minecraft is available on a wide range of platforms, including competing consoles such as Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5, as well as non-Microsoft platforms like Android, iOS, Linux, and Mac.
Why is Call of Duty exempt from Xbox exclusivity?

Microsoft would not make Call of Duty exclusive in this scenario, likely as a result of the 10-year agreement it signed with Nintendo, Nvidia, and Sony in 2023 to keep the franchise on a variety of platforms. That concession was made while Microsoft was seeking regulatory approval for its $68 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Under the terms of that agreement, only Call of Duty is guaranteed to remain multiplatform, not every Activision Blizzard-owned franchise.

If Xbox were to move forward with its drastic new exclusivity plans, it would likely have a noticeable impact on the sales of announced games like The Elder Scrolls 6 and Fallout 5. Developer Bethesda Softworks has generally been platform-agnostic for its key franchises, bringing games like The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim to a wide variety of platforms — a Switch 2 port of the 15-year-old RPG was released just last year.

Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty and CEO Asha Sharma told employees in April that the gaming division's new leadership would reevaluate Xbox's "approach to exclusivity, windowing, and AI." Hot on the heels of news that Xbox timed-exclusive Forza Horizon 6 won't come to PlayStation 5 until 2027 and a special projects group called Xbox Labs that sounds very AI-focused, Booty and Sharma are making good on their new approach.

articles.headline: Lisandro Martinez refuses to apologise as he doubles down on outburst in social media post
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez criticized sporting director Jason Wilcox over squad strengthening following a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.
Martinez defended his comments in a social media post, stating he spoke out of frustration and demanding high standards and ambition from the club.
Manchester United will return to Premier League action on Sunday to face Leeds following a poor start to the season.
body: Lisandro Martinez has doubled down on his frustrations towards Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox.
The Red Devils defender took an almighty swipe at Wilcox for a lack of squad strengthening following the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday.
Martinez did not hold back on his assessment of United following the defeat at the Wanda Metropolitano Getty
talkSPORT understands Martinez is not the only United star frustrated with the perceived lack of ambition at board level.
He has since explained his actions in a lengthy social media post, insisting the club must maintain ‘high standards’ and remain ambitious.
What did Lisandro Martinez say in his statement?
“Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel,” Martinez wrote.
“After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.
“Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win.
“And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

“My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

“When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

“I know that, first and foremost, it’s us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.
“I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.
Wilcox is in the firing line at United following Martinez’s comments Getty
“My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge.”
Manchester United’s summer transfer strategy
This summer presented a prime opportunity for United to strengthen the squad having secured Champions League qualification for the 2026/27 campaign.
But rather than improve across a number of areas, the Red Devils heavily invested in the midfield.
United spent all of their summer transfer budget on Carlos Baleba (£70million), Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m).
The previous summer, more than £200m was spent on forwards Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko.
However, the first choice backline has remained relatively untouched since 2022.
Tielemans has started every Premier League game this season, but Baleba could now end up taking his place Getty
Manchester United’s on-field woes
Martinez’s frustrations with United’s transfer dealings this summer have been exarcebated by a horror start to the 2026/27 Premier League campaign.
A 1-1 draw with Tottenham on Saturday, in which the Red Devils conceded in the 92nd minute, ensured United had their worst start to a league season in 40 years.
Michael Carrick’s side have also been eliminated from the EFL Cup, blowing a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 to Brighton in the third round.
United will look to shake off the midweek chaos when they return to Premier League action on Sunday against rivals Leeds.
